_notes: Locked sprite-type specs for PixelKin. The art source of truth is docs/art-style.md; this file operationalises it for generation. Each type fixes a canvas, grid, anchor, and prompt template. Prompt templates use {subject}, {fw}, {fh}, {cols}, {rows}, {canvas_w}, {canvas_h}, {fill_pct}. The shared _style preamble and _originality clause are prepended to every prompt so all types stay consistent and copyright-clean. DO NOT mention the background colour in templates — the skill owns it: for the default OpenAI gpt-image-2 path it prepends a magenta chroma-key preamble and strips the magenta to transparent in post; for the Google path it uses the native transparent route.
_style: Authentic late-1990s / early-2000s handheld pixel art, in the visual register of a Game Boy Color game growing toward Game Boy Advance. STRICT RULES: hard 1-pixel edges, absolutely NO anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients (a small deliberate dithered pixel gradient is fine). Limited palette of roughly 8-16 colours. A dark outline (deep ink, NOT pure black) around the outer silhouette, lighter internal linework. Consistent light source from the TOP-LEFT. Strong, instantly readable silhouette. Cute, stylised, slightly oversized head and eyes for readability; not realistic, not gritty. Chunky, deliberate square pixels as if drawn pixel-by-pixel on a tiny {fw}x{fh} canvas. No semi-transparent shading. Subject only: no background scenery, no ground, no cast shadow, no frame or border.
_originality: This is original content for PixelKin, a creature-collecting RPG inspired by the genre but a copy of nothing. It must NOT resemble any existing commercial game's creature, character, silhouette, palette signature, logo, font, or UI. Describe by genre and mood only. Make it distinctly original.
_area_style: COHESION: this tile belongs to ONE map area called "{area}" and must read as part of a single unified tile set. Use a shared limited palette of about 10-14 flat colours: {palette}. Keep the SAME pixel density, the SAME top-left light direction, and a matching value range as the rest of the set, so a screen built from these tiles looks like one place and does not visually buzz. Tessellate seamlessly when repeated edge-to-edge; no border, frame, or outline around the tile edge.

creature-front.label: Creature battle front sprite
creature-front.use_for: The forward-facing battle sprite the player sees of an opponent kin.
creature-front.prompt: A single original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, shown as a battle FRONT sprite: a three-quarter front view, facing the viewer in a calm battle-ready idle pose. Subject: {subject}. The creature should fill about {fill_pct}% of the {fw}x{fh} frame, centred horizontally, body base resting near the lower edge so it 'stands' on the ground line. Whole creature in frame, nothing cropped.

creature-back.label: Creature battle back sprite
creature-back.use_for: The rear-view battle sprite of the player's own kin (back turned to the camera).
creature-back.prompt: The SAME original creature seen from BEHIND for a monster-collecting RPG battle back sprite: a three-quarter view from the rear, back turned to the viewer, battle-ready idle pose. Subject: {subject}. It must read as the SAME species as its front sprite — identical palette, proportions and signature features, just viewed from behind. Fills about {fill_pct}% of the {fw}x{fh} frame, centred horizontally, base near the lower edge.

creature-icon.label: Creature menu icon
creature-icon.use_for: Tiny party/box/menu icon for a kin. Head/silhouette focus, must read at 32px.
creature-icon.prompt: A tiny, simplified menu ICON of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, focused on the head and most recognisable silhouette. Subject: {subject}. Drop any fine detail that would vanish at {fw}x{fh}; keep it bold, chunky and instantly readable. Centred in the frame, filling about {fill_pct}%.

creature-overworld.label: Creature overworld mini-sprite
creature-overworld.use_for: A kin roaming the overworld. Very simple, single idle frame by default.
creature-overworld.prompt: A very simple overworld mini-sprite of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG, in a gentle top-down-leaning view, single idle pose. Subject: {subject}. Keep it minimal and charming — readable at {fw}x{fh}, the same species as its battle sprite but simplified. Centred horizontally, feet near the lower edge, filling about {fill_pct}% of the frame.

creature-portrait.label: Creature portrait
creature-portrait.use_for: Larger profile / dex art for a kin. Richer than the battle sprite, same character.
creature-portrait.prompt: A portrait / dex illustration of an original creature for a monster-collecting RPG: a characterful three-quarter front bust or full pose with a touch more colour and detail than the small battle sprite, but the SAME character, palette and personality. Subject: {subject}. Centred in the {fw}x{fh} frame, filling about {fill_pct}%.

human-overworld.label: Human / NPC overworld walk sheet
human-overworld.use_for: A walking character sheet for towns and routes: 3 columns x 4 rows, 32px frames.
human-overworld.prompt: An original human character walking sprite SHEET for a retro monster-collecting RPG, laid out as a strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total). Rows are facing directions top to bottom: row 1 facing DOWN, row 2 facing LEFT, row 3 facing RIGHT, row 4 facing UP. Columns are the walk cycle left to right: column 1 idle stance, column 2 step (left foot forward), column 3 step (right foot forward). Character: {subject}. Keep the head height, proportions and palette identical in every frame — only the legs and arms move. The character must stand on the SAME foot baseline in every cell, centred horizontally, about 20-24px wide inside each 32px frame. Even spacing, each pose isolated in its own cell.

effect.label: Battle effect frame sheet
effect.use_for: A reusable battle effect animation (spark, slash, burst, splash) as a frame grid.
effect.prompt: An original battle EFFECT animation sheet for a retro monster-collecting RPG, laid out as a strict grid of {cols} columns by {rows} rows of {fw}x{fh} frames ({canvas_w}x{canvas_h} total), read left-to-right then top-to-bottom as the animation progresses from start to dissipation. Effect: {subject}. Each frame is one moment of the animation, centred in its cell. Bright, punchy, chunky pixel shapes; no creature or character in the frames — the effect only. Even spacing, one frame per cell.

tile.label: World tile
tile.use_for: A single 16x16 tileable world tile (grass, path, water edge, etc.).
tile.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} world TILE for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG overworld, designed to tessellate seamlessly when repeated edge-to-edge on a grid. Tile: {subject}. Fill the whole {fw}x{fh} frame to the edges (no margin, no outline around the tile border). Keep interior detail low and evenly distributed so a field of these tiles does not visually buzz or show an obvious repeat.

tile-ground.label: Ground fill tile
tile-ground.use_for: A seamless interior ground-fill tile for an area set (grass, dirt, sand, stone floor).
tile-ground.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} GROUND-FILL world tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG, the base surface a player walks on across a whole field. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with low, even interior detail so a large field of these tiles reads as one smooth surface with no obvious seam or repeating hotspot.

tile-path.label: Path / road tile
tile-path.use_for: A seamless path or road tile that tessellates into a walkway through ground tiles.
tile-path.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} PATH tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the trodden walkway surface. Path: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so straight runs of the tile form a continuous path; keep edges neutral so it abuts the area's ground tile cleanly. Low, even detail, no border line around the tile.

tile-water.label: Open water tile
tile-water.use_for: A seamless open-water tile (sea, lake, river body).
tile-water.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} open-WATER tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG. Water: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with a gently rippled surface that tessellates so a large body of water reads as continuous, no obvious repeat. Low, even detail; no shoreline or border in this tile (that is the separate water-edge tile).

tile-water-edge.label: Water/land edge tile
tile-water-edge.use_for: The transition tile where water meets land; pairs with the set's water and ground tiles.
tile-water-edge.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} WATER-EDGE transition tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the boundary where water meets land, with water along one side and shoreline/ground along the other. Edge: {subject}. The water side must tessellate with the set's plain water tile and the land side with the set's ground tile, so it slots between them with no seam. Fill the frame edge-to-edge, no border line.

tile-cliff.label: Cliff / ledge face tile
tile-cliff.use_for: A vertical cliff or ledge face tile (the wall of a height change).
tile-cliff.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} CLIFF-FACE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the vertical rock/earth face of a ledge or height drop, tiling horizontally along a cliff and vertically down a tall face. Face: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge; keep it readable as a solid impassable wall. Low, even detail, no border line.

tile-cliff-edge.label: Cliff top-edge tile
tile-cliff-edge.use_for: The top lip of a cliff where the upper ground meets the cliff face; pairs with cliff + ground.
tile-cliff-edge.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} CLIFF-TOP-EDGE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the lip where upper ground meets the start of a cliff face below. Edge: {subject}. The top must tessellate with the set's ground tile and the bottom with the set's cliff-face tile, so it slots between them. Fill the frame edge-to-edge, no border line.

tile-roof.label: Building roof tile
tile-roof.use_for: A seamless building-roof tile (rendered on the 'above' layer so players pass behind).
tile-roof.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} building-ROOF tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG, tiling across the top of a structure. Roof: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so a roof area reads as continuous; consistent top-left light. Low, even detail, no border line.

tile-wall.label: Building wall tile
tile-wall.use_for: A seamless building/structure wall tile (the solid face below a roof).
tile-wall.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} building-WALL tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: the solid front face of a structure beneath its roof. Wall: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so walls tile horizontally; consistent top-left light. Low, even detail, no border line.

tile-soil.label: Bare soil / dirt ground tile
tile-soil.use_for: A seamless bare-earth ground-fill tile (tilled soil, dirt yard) for an area set.
tile-soil.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} bare SOIL ground-fill world tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: trodden earth a player walks on. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with low, even interior detail so a field of these tiles reads as one continuous earthy surface with no seam or repeating hotspot.

tile-sand.label: Sand ground tile
tile-sand.use_for: A seamless sand ground-fill tile (beach, shore flat) for an area set.
tile-sand.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} SAND ground-fill world tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: soft coastal sand a player walks on. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge with low, even grainy detail so a beach of these tiles reads as one continuous surface with no obvious seam or repeat.

tile-floor.label: Plaza / interior floor tile
tile-floor.use_for: A seamless paved plaza or interior floor fill tile (stone plaza, wood/board floor) for an area or building set.
tile-floor.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} FLOOR fill tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: a paved plaza or board/wood floor a player walks on. Surface: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge; if it has planks or paving, align them so the tile tessellates into a continuous regular floor with no broken seam. Low, even detail, no border line.

tile-door.label: Door tile
tile-door.use_for: A door tile set into a wall (an entrance the player faces); fills its frame, abuts the wall tile.
tile-door.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} DOOR tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: a closed doorway set into a building wall, viewed head-on. Door: {subject}. Fill the frame edge-to-edge so the surrounding wall material matches the set's wall tile and the door sits centred within it; consistent top-left light. Low, even detail, no border line around the tile.

tile-fence.label: Fence / railing tile
tile-fence.use_for: A fence or railing tile that tiles horizontally to bound a yard or dock; transparent above the rail.
tile-fence.prompt: A single original {fw}x{fh} FENCE tile for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG: a low wooden fence or railing seen from the front, the rail running horizontally so a row of these tiles forms one continuous fence. Fence: {subject}. The rail sits in the lower-middle of the tile with transparent space above it; the posts align so the tile repeats horizontally with no break. Consistent top-left light, dark non-black outline.

tile-decor.label: Decoration tile
tile-decor.use_for: A small standalone decoration that sits on a deco layer over ground (flower, sign, crate, lamp). Keeps transparency around it.
tile-decor.prompt: A single small original {fw}x{fh} DECORATION object for a retro top-down monster-collecting RPG overworld, sitting alone so it can be placed over a ground tile (transparent around the object, NOT a full edge-to-edge surface). Object: {subject}. Centred in the frame, chunky and readable at {fw}x{fh}, consistent top-left light, dark non-black outline.
